title: The Village Wi-Fi War
synopsis: When a mysterious internet signal suddenly appears in a tiny village, everyone becomes obsessed with getting the password. Two reckless friends accidentally start a war between the villagers, a local chief, and a very angry technician.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: In the quiet village of Umuoba, nothing exciting had happened for years. Then one afternoon, Tobi discovered something more powerful than common sense: a mysterious Wi-Fi signal coming from the old hut near the village square.

scenes.speaker: tobi
scenes.text: Emeka, look! My phone says there is free Wi-Fi. Free! Do you understand what this means? We can finally watch videos without begging somebody for data.

scenes.speaker: emeka
scenes.text: Calm down. Nothing in this village is free. Last week Mama Rose charged me just to stand near her shop because I was blocking the sunlight.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The boys approached the hut like professional spies, despite having absolutely no experience as spies. The signal was strong, the door was locked, and somebody inside was loudly snoring.

scenes.speaker: tobi
scenes.text: We need the password. Maybe it is written somewhere. Check the table. Check the wall. Check the chief's dignity. That last one might be easier.

scenes.speaker: emeka
scenes.text: I found something. The password is written on this paper. It says: ChiefBubaIsTheBest123.

scenes.speaker: chief
scenes.text: WHO gave you boys permission to touch my internet?

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: By sunset, the entire village knew about the Wi-Fi. Nobody knew where it came from, but everybody had an opinion. This was now the most important political issue the village had ever seen.

scenes.speaker: mama
scenes.text: Chief, I am telling you now: if that internet remains free, my shop will suffer. People are already sitting outside and buying nothing except one sachet of water.

scenes.speaker: chief
scenes.text: Nobody will use my Wi-Fi without paying the village development fee. I am thinking of charging by the minute.

scenes.speaker: tobi
scenes.text: That is ridiculous. The internet belongs to everybody. Also, I already changed the password, so technically I am now the Minister of Wi-Fi.

scenes.speaker: emeka
scenes.text: You changed the password? What did you change it to?

scenes.speaker: tobi
scenes.text: Password123. I wanted something nobody could guess.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Within ten minutes, every person in the village was connected. Then every phone stopped working. The mysterious signal had suddenly disappeared, and somewhere in the distance, an angry technician was walking toward the village.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The next morning, Kola arrived carrying a cane and the expression of a man who had discovered that several strangers were using his internet without permission. Nobody knew who he was, but everyone immediately blamed Tobi.

scenes.speaker: kola
scenes.text: Who touched my router? I installed that connection for one customer. Somehow fifty-seven people are now connected. One of them is downloading something enormous.

scenes.speaker: emeka
scenes.text: It was not us. We only connected the village, changed the password, and accidentally caused the internet to disappear.

scenes.speaker: tobi
scenes.text: Why are you looking at me? You were the one who pressed the button.

scenes.speaker: kola
scenes.text: Enough. The router is overloaded. Somebody has connected every phone, television, and suspicious device in this village.

scenes.speaker: chief
scenes.text: Can you fix it before the village discovers that I promised free internet during my next speech?

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Kola looked at the broken connection, then at Tobi and Emeka. He had seen this kind of disaster before. But never this stupid. He made one final decision: the boys would help fix it.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: The repair plan was simple: reconnect the machine, restart the signal, and stop the entire village from touching anything. Unfortunately, the village had already gathered around the machine to offer advice nobody had requested.

scenes.speaker: mama
scenes.text: I know what the problem is. You need to hit it three times. That works for my radio, my blender, and my husband.

scenes.speaker: kola
scenes.text: Please do not hit the machine. This equipment costs more than this entire village.

scenes.speaker: tobi
scenes.text: What if we turn it off and on again?

scenes.speaker: kola
scenes.text: That is literally the first thing I tried.

scenes.speaker: chief
scenes.text: Everybody move back. As chief, I have decided to solve this personally.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Chief Buba reached toward the machine. Nobody breathed. Then he pressed the only button that had a warning label. The entire room went dark, followed by one enormous flash.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: When the smoke cleared, the internet was back. The village cheered. Tobi smiled proudly. Emeka looked suspiciously at the machine. Chief Buba prepared a speech. Then every phone in the village received the same message.

scenes.speaker: emeka
scenes.text: Guys... I think we just received a bill.

scenes.speaker: tobi
scenes.text: How much?

scenes.speaker: emeka
scenes.text: Enough to buy the village twice.

scenes.speaker: chief
scenes.text: Nobody panic. I have a solution. We will simply create a village internet tax.

scenes.speaker: mama
scenes.text: You cannot tax the internet! You already taxed the market, the goats, and my chair outside the shop.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.text: Everyone began shouting at once. Tobi quietly looked at Emeka. Emeka looked back. They both smiled. Somewhere behind them, the Wi-Fi signal appeared again, stronger than ever. And this time, the password was already public.
